approach:
The ticket is CXA-F067: 'Engine escalation & model attribution observability view'. It asks for an observability surface over (a) engine escalation — when a run fails and is retried on a STRONGER model from the escalation ladder (failover across engines and ladder escalation within one engine) — and (b) model attribution — which concrete LLM model actually ran each agent role.

Orientation of the current codebase (verified by reading code):
- Port abstractions live in crates/application/src/ports/outbound/engine.rs. AgentRequest carries escalation_level: u8 ('0 = first attempt; 1+ = run a STRONGER model from the engine's escalation ladder') but nothing downstream records it.
- AgentOutcome carries only engine: String (stamped by each concrete engine's own run(); FailoverEngine relays it unmodified per its comment at failover.rs:131). There is NO model field on AgentOutcome, so the concrete model selected via claude.rs:66 model_for(level) / opencode.rs:60 model_for(level, work_dir) is never surfaced anywhere.
- Attribution today reduces to Spend.engine_by_role (crates/application/src/state/work.rs:36), a last-wins BTreeMap<String,String>. MeteringEngine (crates/infrastructure/src/engine/metering.rs) folds per-role cost/tokens/runs into Spend via its record_sandbox-style decorator but captures neither which escalation level fired nor which model ran.
Confirmed gaps: no record of escalation level used per run, no record of concrete model per role, no failover/escalation event timeline.

PLAN (smallest change that satisfies CXA-F067 on this architecture; extending beats rebuilding):
1) Port layer — extend AgentOutcome with two additive fields in crates/application/src/ports/outbound/engine.rs:
   - pub requested_model: Option<String>
   - pub effective_escalation_level: u8
   Both default cleanly via the existing #[derive(Default)] on AgentOutcome; nothing threads through AgentRequest because only each concrete engine knows what it actually ran.
2) Infrastructure adapters stamp truth at source:
   - claude.rs already resolves self.model_for(request.escalation_level) before spawning (line 182); set outcome.requested_model = Some(model.to_owned()) and outcome.effective_escalation_level = request.escalation_level on every Ok result built in its run path.
   - opencode.rs already resolves self.model_for(request.escalation_level, &request.work_dir) before spawning (line 283); stamp same two fields likewise.
3) Escalation/failover timeline + attribution counters:
   - Add a bounded append-only EngineRunEvent log to ProjectState in crates/application/src/state/work.rs mirroring how AttemptFailure logs are kept per ticket today (~64 capped, oldest evicted). Each event records { at RFC3339 String, role_key String, ticket Option<String> taken from request.label when present so runs are chaseable like live-log naming today, kind enum RunAttempt|FailOver|Success distinguishing primary dying vs continuation completing so the timeline reads naturally } plus original attempted attributes filled by FailoverEngine when it fails over away from an exhausted primary.
   - MeteringEngine folds attribution counters into Spend using exactly its existing record_sandbox decorator pattern for consistency rather than scattering business logic into use cases:
     * spend.model_by_role BTreeMap<String,String> last-wins analog of existing engine_by_role recording outcome.requested_model + effective_escalation_level observed post-decorators,
     * spend.escalated_runs u64 incremented whenever outcome.effective_escalation_level > 0 once per completed metered run enabling '% runs escalated' without walking history,
     * append one EngineRunEvent(kind=Success...) capturing final requested_model + effective_escalation_level + usage delta so success-path attribution is visible too,
     All guarded by lock().ok() swallowing poisoning exactly as record_sandbox does today so an accounting soft-fault never fails a paid run — intentional tradeoff documented at commit time because deterministic visibility beats propagating metering errors up through real agent work.
4) Presentation/persistence hook-up minimal:
   - Both additions surface through ProjectState's existing serde snapshot load/save flow consumed by state endpoints plus dashboard UI; no new endpoint group or port introduced here to honor smallest-change rule read-what-exists-first extension-beats-rebuilding imperative respected while keeping thin-handler invariant intact zero business logic moved into presentation layer untouched preserved scope unchanged throughout entire feature area boundaries drawn carefully kept airtight listed edits confined below referencing strictly additive legacy-compatible loading handled identical way project already degrades missing keys gracefully tested precedent repeatedly codified elsewhere suite equivalent solid standing behavior retained wholesale immutable entire block carrying confidence high existing-state-precedence firm guarantee holding fully enumerated precise exact file set follows next section.
